page.overview:
Who is Harold Hadley Copeland?

Prof. Harold Hadley Copeland is a fictional character created by Lin Carter for his Cthulhu Mythos short story "The Dweller in the Tomb".

Prof. Copeland was an eminent archaeologist, one of the world's leading authorities on ancient civilisations of the Pacific area. He co-founded the Pacific Area Archaeological Association and was, at some point, president of it, prior to his compulsory resignation in 1911. While his earlier works were lauded as brilliant, Copeland's interest in unorthodox hypotheses, such as touching upon the existence and worship of Cthulhu and particularly about the existence of the lost continent of Mu, led to the gradual decline of his reputation.

His Prehistory in the Pacific: A Preliminary Investigation with Reference to the Myth Patterns of Southeast Asia (1902) was universally admired and acclaimed. Polynesian Mythology, with a Note on the Cthulhu Legend Cycle (1906) was more controversial, but still regarded as "a massive work of scientific research". However, after reading the Ponape Scripture, Copeland became obsessed with finding the tomb of Zanthu, a hierophant who escaped the destruction of Mu, and the legendary Zanthu Tablets. His next published book, The Prehistoric Pacific in the Light of the Ponape Scripture (1911), resulted in his being asked to resign from the Pacific Area Archaeological Association.

After his academic fall from grace, Copeland organised the Copeland-Ellington expedition to central Asia, which penetrated the Plateau of Tsang in 1913 to search for the tomb of Zanthu. Ellington died of red-water fever only a few days after the party's departure from Sangup-Koy, leaving Copeland as the solo leader. Deep into the inhospitable deserts of Tsang, other members of the expedition deserted or were taken one by one by the Mi-Go. Copeland felt an inexplicable familiarity with the Plateau, as if he had seen it before in a previous life or in dreams. When confronted by a Mi-Go, he was even more surprised to find that the creature appeared to recognise him, and it was the Mi-Go who was scared of him, rather than vice-versa.
